claims.text: The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy has enhanced strength at 100–200 °C and strain rates of 10^-2–10^-1 s^-1 relative to room temperature and low strain rates.
The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy has enhanced ductility at 100–200 °C and strain rates of 10^-2–10^-1 s^-1 relative to room temperature and low strain rates.
Optimized lattice-strain relaxation causes the proposed enhancement in strength and ductility.
Dislocation absorption causes the proposed enhancement in strength and ductility.
Grain rotation causes the proposed enhancement in strength and ductility.
The alloy's chemical complexity and lattice distortion influence lattice-strain relaxation, dislocation behavior, and grain rotation.
The relevant material is in a solid-solution state.
Pre-deformed and non-pre-deformed initial states are both within the proposed test regime.
Changing temperature and strain rate will alter lattice-strain evolution.
Changing temperature and strain rate will alter dislocation accumulation.
Changing temperature and strain rate will alter grain rotation.
Room-temperature, low-strain-rate behavior provides the baseline for comparison.
In-situ neutron diffraction and transmission electron microscopy during tensile deformation can be used to track lattice strain, dislocation density, and grain-structure evolution.

contradictions.description: The proposed dislocation mediator is described variously as dislocation absorption and dislocation accumulation, without explaining how these distinct or potentially opposing processes are reconciled or which one should be observed.
